- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.

- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).

- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).

- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.

item.text:
# `packages/report-ui` Cleanup Plan

## Summary
- The main problem is not “too few abstractions.” It is that the package has no clean seam between routes, data sources, session-state derivation, and rendering.
- `ReviewSessionPage.tsx` is the worst offender: it currently behaves like two apps jammed into one file, with a mock app and a real app sharing names but not architecture.
- The package is also still carrying dead report-era UI and a second styling approach, which keeps the current Studio direction harder to reason about than it should be.

## Blunt Audit
- Routing is mixed with view logic. The launch page owns redirects, current-session handoff, and start-event navigation inside the page component. The session page switches mock vs real at the top-level export instead of below a stable route boundary.
- Mock concerns are mixed with product concerns. `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK` reaches deep into page files, and large mock builders plus fake progression logic live beside real JSX.
- Data loading and state transitions are mixed directly into page components. The session page owns aggregate fetch, activity subscription, policy approval, adopt, local diff loading, merge-back, and terminal-state derivation.
- UI duplication exists between mock and real paths. The stage/status UI, findings, console, reviewed diff, adopt, local changes, merge-back, and outcome sections are effectively rendered twice.
- File boundaries are wrong. `ReviewSessionPage.tsx`, `ReviewHistoryPage.tsx`, `lib/review.ts`, `types.ts`, and `styles.css` are all acting as dumping grounds.
- Current component boundaries do not make sense. `App.tsx` is fine; the page files are not. They are route, controller, adapter, and screen all at once.
- The package still contains dead report-era surfaces and tests. Since the desired direction is session-first Studio, that dead surface should be removed, not preserved.

## Target Architecture
- Keep `App.tsx` as a two-route table only: compact launch route and session route. No app-shell expansion, no broad history browser, no drift back to reports.
- For each route, split into three layers: a thin route/container, a controller hook, and a pure screen component.
- Add a thin `StudioDataSource` interface for product-level operations. Real and mock implementations must both satisfy it. `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK` should only choose the default implementation at bootstrap.
- Add a thin `SessionViewModel` adapter. Yes, there should be an adapter layer, but it should be boring and one-way: raw session domain state in, exact screen model out.
- Keep one rendering path for live and mock. A mocked session should render through the exact same screen tree as a live session.
- Rename the page concepts to match the product: `StudioLaunchPage` and `StudioSessionPage`. `ReviewHistoryPage` is a misleading name for the current direction.

## Recommended Module Breakdown
- `src/features/studio-launch/`: route/container, controller hook, pure screen, launch-specific leaf UI.
- `src/features/studio-session/`: route/container, controller hook, `sessionViewModel`, and focused panels for stage, activity, findings, reviewed diff, adopt, local changes, merge-back, and terminal outcome.
- `src/data/studio/`: `StudioDataSource`, `realStudioDataSource`, `mockStudioDataSource`, and small scripted mock scenarios.
- `src/domain/studio/`: contracts and parsers split by concern: launch, session aggregate, activity, diff/local changes, adopt/merge-back.
- `src/styles/`: `base.css`, `studio-launch.css`, `studio-session.css`. Keep plain CSS; do not introduce a new styling system.

## Interface Changes
- Add `StudioDataSource` with methods equivalent to: load launch context, start session, load session, subscribe to session activity, approve policy, load local diff, adopt, merge-back.
- Add `buildSessionViewModel(domainState)` to centralize active vs terminal truth, action availability, panel visibility, and user-facing session status text.
- Keep backend contract parsing out of JSX. Raw API shapes should stop leaking directly into page render code.

## Mock Strategy
- Delete the idea of a “mock page.” Keep only a mock data source.
- Mock progression should be a scripted timeline in the data source, not JSX-side orchestration.
- Mock and real should share the same controller and the same screen components.
- Tests should inject a data source directly. `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK` should be app-start wiring only, not a component-level branch.
- Keep the mock catalog intentionally small: happy path, human-approval gate, terminal failure, merge-back complete.

## Phased Cleanup Plan
1. Establish the seam: introduce `StudioDataSource`, move `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK` selection to bootstrap, and make mock and real session flows render through one shared session screen. Acceptance: no page component branches on `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK`.
2. Extract the session controller and view model: move fetch/subscription/actions out of the session screen, centralize active/terminal/adopt/merge-back rules in `buildSessionViewModel`, and split the session screen into focused panels. Acceptance: session JSX reads like layout code, not orchestration code.
3. Clean up the launch route: rename it to match the product, move preflight/start/current-session/navigation logic into a controller, and keep the route compact. Acceptance: the launch screen is small, readable, and no longer mixes routing with rendering.
4. Break up contracts and tests: split `lib/review.ts` and `types.ts` by Studio concern, add focused parser and view-model tests, and replace stale page tests with behavior-driven tests against controllers/screens. Acceptance: basic session behavior no longer requires giant page-level fetch/EventSource mocks.
5. Clean the CSS the boring way: split feature CSS, tighten selector naming, and remove generic cross-feature styles. Acceptance: launch/session styling is obviously scoped and there is one surviving styling approach.
6. Delete the old report world: remove dead report-era components, tests, and style residue, then clean up adjacent route leftovers in CLI/static serving. Acceptance: `report-ui` contains only the current Studio product surface.

## Test Plan
- Parser tests for each Studio contract group.
- `SessionViewModel` tests for active, policy-pending, failed, adopt-ready, and merge-back-complete states.
- Data-source contract tests proving real and mock expose the same behavior shape.
- Route/controller integration tests for launch, session resume, session subscribe/refresh, and start-session navigation.
- Pure screen tests using injected view models instead of page-level network orchestration.

## Real Blockers / Contract Gaps
- Some CLI Studio entrypoints still open `/` instead of the concrete session route for session-backed launches. That is real adjacent cleanup and should be fixed before calling the old report path fully dead.
- Static UI serving still special-cases `/reports/`. Remove that only when all callers are updated.
- There is no obvious backend schema blocker inside `report-ui`; the current Studio responses are sufficient once normalized in one place.

## What I Would Do First
- First slice: add `StudioDataSource` and `buildSessionViewModel`, then force both mock and real session flows through one shared `StudioSessionScreen`. That is the highest-leverage cut in the whole package.

## Assumptions / Defaults
- Keep the package name for now; clean the internals before debating package renames.
- Preserve the session-first model, the `adopt` term, explicit human approval at adopt/merge-back, and honesty about active vs terminal state.
- Delete legacy report-era surfaces rather than preserving them behind dead code.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.

# `packages/report-ui` Cleanup Plan

## Summary
- The main problem is not “too few abstractions.” It is that the package has no clean seam between routes, data sources, session-state derivation, and rendering.
- `ReviewSessionPage.tsx` is the worst offender: it currently behaves like two apps jammed into one file, with a mock app and a real app sharing names but not architecture.
- The package is also still carrying dead report-era UI and a second styling approach, which keeps the current Studio direction harder to reason about than it should be.

## Blunt Audit
- Routing is mixed with view logic. The launch page owns redirects, current-session handoff, and start-event navigation inside the page component. The session page switches mock vs real at the top-level export instead of below a stable route boundary.
- Mock concerns are mixed with product concerns. `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK` reaches deep into page files, and large mock builders plus fake progression logic live beside real JSX.
- Data loading and state transitions are mixed directly into page components. The session page owns aggregate fetch, activity subscription, policy approval, adopt, local diff loading, merge-back, and terminal-state derivation.
- UI duplication exists between mock and real paths. The stage/status UI, findings, console, reviewed diff, adopt, local changes, merge-back, and outcome sections are effectively rendered twice.
- File boundaries are wrong. `ReviewSessionPage.tsx`, `ReviewHistoryPage.tsx`, `lib/review.ts`, `types.ts`, and `styles.css` are all acting as dumping grounds.
- Current component boundaries do not make sense. `App.tsx` is fine; the page files are not. They are route, controller, adapter, and screen all at once.
- The package still contains dead report-era surfaces and tests. Since the desired direction is session-first Studio, that dead surface should be removed, not preserved.

## Target Architecture
- Keep `App.tsx` as a two-route table only: compact launch route and session route. No app-shell expansion, no broad history browser, no drift back to reports.
- For each route, split into three layers: a thin route/container, a controller hook, and a pure screen component.
- Add a thin `StudioDataSource` interface for product-level operations. Real and mock implementations must both satisfy it. `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK` should only choose the default implementation at bootstrap.
- Add a thin `SessionViewModel` adapter. Yes, there should be an adapter layer, but it should be boring and one-way: raw session domain state in, exact screen model out.
- Keep one rendering path for live and mock. A mocked session should render through the exact same screen tree as a live session.
- Rename the page concepts to match the product: `StudioLaunchPage` and `StudioSessionPage`. `ReviewHistoryPage` is a misleading name for the current direction.

## Recommended Module Breakdown
- `src/features/studio-launch/`: route/container, controller hook, pure screen, launch-specific leaf UI.
- `src/features/studio-session/`: route/container, controller hook, `sessionViewModel`, and focused panels for stage, activity, findings, reviewed diff, adopt, local changes, merge-back, and terminal outcome.
- `src/data/studio/`: `StudioDataSource`, `realStudioDataSource`, `mockStudioDataSource`, and small scripted mock scenarios.
- `src/domain/studio/`: contracts and parsers split by concern: launch, session aggregate, activity, diff/local changes, adopt/merge-back.
- `src/styles/`: `base.css`, `studio-launch.css`, `studio-session.css`. Keep plain CSS; do not introduce a new styling system.

## Interface Changes
- Add `StudioDataSource` with methods equivalent to: load launch context, start session, load session, subscribe to session activity, approve policy, load local diff, adopt, merge-back.
- Add `buildSessionViewModel(domainState)` to centralize active vs terminal truth, action availability, panel visibility, and user-facing session status text.
- Keep backend contract parsing out of JSX. Raw API shapes should stop leaking directly into page render code.

## Mock Strategy
- Delete the idea of a “mock page.” Keep only a mock data source.
- Mock progression should be a scripted timeline in the data source, not JSX-side orchestration.
- Mock and real should share the same controller and the same screen components.
- Tests should inject a data source directly. `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK` should be app-start wiring only, not a component-level branch.
- Keep the mock catalog intentionally small: happy path, human-approval gate, terminal failure, merge-back complete.

## Phased Cleanup Plan
1. Establish the seam: introduce `StudioDataSource`, move `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK` selection to bootstrap, and make mock and real session flows render through one shared session screen. Acceptance: no page component branches on `VITE_STUDIO_MOCK`.
2. Extract the session controller and view model: move fetch/subscription/actions out of the session screen, centralize active/terminal/adopt/merge-back rules in `buildSessionViewModel`, and split the session screen into focused panels. Acceptance: session JSX reads like layout code, not orchestration code.
3. Clean up the launch route: rename it to match the product, move preflight/start/current-session/navigation logic into a controller, and keep the route compact. Acceptance: the launch screen is small, readable, and no longer mixes routing with rendering.
4. Break up contracts and tests: split `lib/review.ts` and `types.ts` by Studio concern, add focused parser and view-model tests, and replace stale page tests with behavior-driven tests against controllers/screens. Acceptance: basic session behavior no longer requires giant page-level fetch/EventSource mocks.
5. Clean the CSS the boring way: split feature CSS, tighten selector naming, and remove generic cross-feature styles. Acceptance: launch/session styling is obviously scoped and there is one surviving styling approach.
6. Delete the old report world: remove dead report-era components, tests, and style residue, then clean up adjacent route leftovers in CLI/static serving. Acceptance: `report-ui` contains only the current Studio product surface.

## Test Plan
- Parser tests for each Studio contract group.
- `SessionViewModel` tests for active, policy-pending, failed, adopt-ready, and merge-back-complete states.
- Data-source contract tests proving real and mock expose the same behavior shape.
- Route/controller integration tests for launch, session resume, session subscribe/refresh, and start-session navigation.
- Pure screen tests using injected view models instead of page-level network orchestration.

## Real Blockers / Contract Gaps
- Some CLI Studio entrypoints still open `/` instead of the concrete session route for session-backed launches. That is real adjacent cleanup and should be fixed before calling the old report path fully dead.
- Static UI serving still special-cases `/reports/`. Remove that only when all callers are updated.
- There is no obvious backend schema blocker inside `report-ui`; the current Studio responses are sufficient once normalized in one place.

## What I Would Do First
- First slice: add `StudioDataSource` and `buildSessionViewModel`, then force both mock and real session flows through one shared `StudioSessionScreen`. That is the highest-leverage cut in the whole package.

## Assumptions / Defaults
- Keep the package name for now; clean the internals before debating package renames.
- Preserve the session-first model, the `adopt` term, explicit human approval at adopt/merge-back, and honesty about active vs terminal state.
- Delete legacy report-era surfaces rather than preserving them behind dead code.

payload.message:
**Implemented**
`packages/report-ui` now uses the architecture from the plan instead of the old page-monolith setup. The app boots a single studio data source in [main.tsx](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/main.tsx) and routes only to the compact launch page and the session page in [App.tsx](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/App.tsx). Launch and session now each have a thin page, a controller hook, and a shared screen tree in [StudioLaunchPage.tsx](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/features/studio-launch/StudioLaunchPage.tsx), [useStudioLaunchController.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/features/studio-launch/useStudioLaunchController.ts), [StudioSessionPage.tsx](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/features/studio-session/StudioSessionPage.tsx), [useStudioSessionController.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/features/studio-session/useStudioSessionController.ts), and [sessionViewModel.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/features/studio-session/sessionViewModel.ts).

Mocks are no longer a second UI. They now live behind the shared data-source seam in [StudioDataSource.tsx](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/data/studio/StudioDataSource.tsx), [realStudioDataSource.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/data/studio/realStudioDataSource.ts), and [mockStudioDataSource.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/data/studio/mockStudioDataSource.ts). The contract layer is split into [domain/review](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/domain/review) and [domain/studio](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/domain/studio), and CSS is split into [base.css](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/styles/base.css), [studio-launch.css](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/styles/studio-launch.css), and [studio-session.css](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/styles/studio-session.css). I also removed the old report-era components, tests, utility files, and the unused shadcn-style UI layer.

**Adjacent cleanup**
The CLI handoff paths now align with the session-only UI. Session-backed launches open `/sessions/:id`, and the leftover report-route fallback logic was removed from [create-from-commit.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/create-from-commit.ts), [create-from-deployment.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/create-from-deployment.ts), [studio-create.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts), [create-shared.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/create-shared.ts), and [ui-static.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-static.ts).

**Verification**

- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-report-ui test`
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-report-ui build`
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus build`

I left the unrelated existing changes in `.codex/skills/...` and `docs/architecture/review-session-pivot.md` alone.
